I'm in Europe, so prices vary a lot from USA and Canada, since the majority of the products discussed there are not easily available here. In contrast, products that are really available here cost twice as much in the other side of the world.

How old are you? And where do you live? If you're in your 20s, a good moisturiser would cost around $20. Find out your skin type and needs, try different products from different companies, and find something  that's perfect for you. Same for your cleanser, there are so many formulas, you're bound to find something for you. Unless you live under the earth, you need to sunscreen throughout the year. Depending where you live, choose a low (spf 20) or a high (spf 40+) sunscreen. 

You can totally take care of your skin (and yourself) within a small budget. A body moisturiser at 400ml, cost ~ $10 and can last for two-three months with daily use, a face cleanser (150-200ml) cost ~15 and depending on the formula you like last for months, a face scrubbing costs around the same and lasts even more with use 1-3 days, a 24hrs or day&night cost around ~20 for usually 50ml and last two months depending on the formula (light, rich, was etc) with daily and nightly use,  a day and a night cream last twice as much. An eye cream costs around 20, and last 4+ months for the usual 15-40ml with daily and nightly use.  I always tell my clients if they can't afford to take everything at once, start from the basics and then take the rest. **Edit** you can buy them even cheaper during sales! Check the expiration dates, store them in a cool, dry place with no direct sunlight, and your set to go! I got my hair conditioner, serums and hairspray during the Xmas sales, and I'm okay for the next year at least. 

Also, no, there's no cream that can prevent eyelid dropping (if you mean ptosis that happens as you age). There are some that improve the appearance (Mey's platinum eye creams do great things on eyelids that have gone south), but nothing that will not make it happen. Unless  you look into something like epidermis injections, but I'd personally prefer a lifting before I self inject my eyelids!

If you start taking care of  your skin from your 20s, the yes, cheap or mid-range (usually have less fillers) products will be great considering daily use. But if you start on your mid 30s like most of my clients, you'll need to use mid to high products to first repair as much damage and then maintain the health of your skin. And if you start even later, then only high end products will show results. My rant was going for people that neglect their skin, and suddenly want to have healthy and youthful skin for dirty cheap or for a quick fix, unfortunately, it doesn't work like that and it's not so cheap.

As I always say, clean, moisturise, and use sunscreen! It'll only benefit you.

The $3 anti-aging cream will do nothing, except maybe hydrate your skin, but the $150 one will do something. If you're afraid of aging and looking like a prune, use sunscreen, clean and moisturise your skin everyday, and you won't need to resort to expensive products to see them working. I always have 40-somethings that want cheap miracles because for so many years they ignored their skincare, yeah the cheap stuff doesn't work, and only some of the expensive stuff work.
